abject

/AB-jekt/ - the stress falls on AB · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Abject means wretched, pitiful.

Sailors rescued from the drifting lifeboat were in an abject state: sunburned, silent, and too weak to climb the ladder unaided.

Example

Inspectors who finally entered the shuttered roadside zoo found the animals in abject misery — cages ankle-deep in filth, water dishes bone dry, a bear pacing a concrete cell barely longer than itself.

Abject is stronger than 'poor' or 'miserable' because it means misery at the very bottom, with dignity stripped away. The same idea of being 'thrown down' lets it intensify other low states too: an abject apology, an abject failure.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

squalid: Squalid describes filthy, degraded surroundings — a squalid room, a squalid alley. Abject covers a person's whole condition: misery so complete that dignity is gone. A place is squalid; a person, an apology, or a failure is abject.

destitute: Destitute means utterly without money or the basic necessities of life, and it measures what a person materially lacks. Abject measures how completely misery has crushed someone — an abject figure may still have shelter yet has lost all dignity. Destitute counts possessions; abject weighs the whole condition.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

dignified: hardship may remain, but self-respect stands

comfortable: materially secure, with nothing wretched in sight

Where it sits · how completely misery strips away dignity

shabby → wretched → abject

shabby vs. abject: Shabby is far milder than abject — a shabby coat is merely worn and frayed, and nothing about it suggests real misery.

wretched vs. abject: Wretched is weaker than abject — wretched names deep misery, while abject strips away the last of a person's comfort and dignity as well.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — ab-: away, down

Root — ject: to throw (Latin iacere)

Put it together: Ab- (away, down) + ject (to throw) = thrown down. Someone in an abject state has been cast down as low as a person can go — which is why the word attaches to bottom-of-the-scale miseries: abject poverty, abject terror, an abject apology offered from the floor.

Use the root in a new word: eject: When the engine caught fire, the pilot had half a second to decide whether to eject.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / literary

Reach for abject when misery is total and dignity is gone — abject poverty, an abject apology, an abject failure. For ordinary hardship, 'poor' or 'miserable' is enough. Its unit-mates divide this territory: forlorn is lonely and hopeless, bereft has lost one precious thing, but abject has lost everything down to self-respect.
